tm_reasoning: NYC mixed climate + office schedule: occupied 06–18 with cooling at 23.9 °C pins indoor near 23–24 °C; nights/weekends setback lets the room drift cooler in winter (down toward 16–19 °C) and warmer in summer evenings. At pos4 the interface temperature tracks indoor closely (insulation isolates outdoors).

To reduce occupied cooling energy, Tm should sit within/just below the indoor band so latent absorption occurs during afternoon gains. A 4 °C band around Tm = 22 °C ([20,24] °C) overlaps the occupied indoor range, enabling melting during late day without needing indoor to exceed 24 °C appreciably.

Night/shoulder re-solidification feasibility: with heating setback to 15.6 °C and frequent cool nights in NYC, the pos4 interface can drop below ~20 °C often enough to refreeze, restoring capacity for the next day; higher Tm (e.g., 26 °C) risks poor refreezing and under-cycling at this interior-coupled node [dc157b807f74f266940a34f671935070__image__0012].

Mechanism evidence: interior-adjacent PCM in temperate/oceanic-like conditions favors cooling reduction when Tm ≈ 20–24 °C [rule_01_oceanic_interior_favors_cooling]; mid-wall data show higher Tt (≈26 °C) cycles weakly when the interface swing is small, reinforcing the choice of a lower Tm for reliable cycling [dc157b807f74f266940a34f671935070__image__0012].

Material family with 200 kJ/kg offers variants at 18/21/23/25/29 °C; prior façade studies found PCM25 best in a warmer Marmara case, but under NYC’s tighter daytime setpoint control a slightly lower Tm (22 °C) better aligns with the occupied band and nightly refreeze needs [3fc0212289cc39ffae6bae56c80890b2__table__0001, case_wall_south].
final.joint_rationale: Placing the PCM at the insulation/inner-gypsum interface (pos4) maximizes coupling to the room—most wall R is outside the PCM—so latent events directly offset HVAC loads. Selecting Tm = 22 °C aligns the 4 °C phase band with the occupied indoor range to absorb afternoon gains, while NYC’s cool nights and winter/shoulder setbacks enable refreezing, maintaining daily capacity.
reasoning_chain: Wall R distribution: insulation R≈1.65 m²K/W dominates (>80% of total), so interfaces exterior to the insulation (pos0–pos2) are weakly coupled to the room; pos4, just inside the insulation, is strongly coupled (only inner gypsum between PCM and zone). First-principles coupling via R-ratio (retrieval gap: no explicit proximity rule retrieved for this exact assembly).

NYC HSCW climate + office schedule yields: large outdoor diurnal swings; occupied hours hold 23–24 °C; setbacks permit night/weekend drift (cool in winter, warm in summer). Thus, pos4 sees small but useful swings near the indoor setpoints; pos0–pos2 see large swings but are separated from the room by the full insulation R.

Eliminate pos3 (mid-insulation): center-of-wall PCM shows weak sensitivity of annual loads to Tt and higher Tt under-cycles when temperature swing is small; mechanism confirmed in a year-long X=0.5 study [dc157b807f74f266940a34f671935070__image__0012].

Exterior-biased placements (pos0/pos1/pos2) can intercept summer gains but are decoupled by the insulation and risk winter penalties in mixed climates; external-layer optima near 30 °C reported for severe-cold summers [case_Harbin] and hot climates [case_01_pcm_parametric_types_thickness_positions, rule_1], but those conditions/walls differ from NYC mixed and our insulated assembly—thus not preferred for total annual energy.

Interior-adjacent PCM (analogous to PCM at the interior face of insulation) reduces heat-flux amplitudes when Tm is suitably chosen for season/orientation [case_03_pcm_config1_winter_summer]; review-level synthesis suggests interior/between-insulation with Tm ≈ 20–24 °C favors cooling and peak reduction in temperate/oceanic-like scenarios with cool nights [rule_01_oceanic_interior_favors_cooling].

Within pos4, higher Tm (≈26 °C) risks limited daily cycling under daytime setpoint control (supported by mid-wall cycling evidence [dc157b...]); choosing Tm = 22 °C (band 20–24 °C) matches occupied indoor temperatures for daytime latent absorption and leverages setback-driven cool nights for refreezing; PCM family properties at these Tm values match the 200 kJ/kg specification [3fc0212289cc39ffae6bae56c80890b2__table__0001].

Cross-check against warmer Marmara case with interior-near PCM: PCM25 performed best there but schedule/climate differ (Csa vs NYC Dfa/Cfa); mechanism is consistent that Tm near indoor cooling band is effective; NYC’s tighter 23.9 °C control favors slightly lower Tm to ensure cycling and refreeze [case_wall_south].

alternatives.why_not_preferred: Tm=24 °C (band 22–26 °C) aligns with cooling setpoint but risks insufficient nightly refreezing under NYC summers, reducing phase-cycling depth; mid-wall evidence shows higher Tt cycles less when swings are small, suggesting similar risk at an interior-coupled node under tight daytime control.

Exterior side of insulation with high Tm can intercept summer gains [case_Harbin, rule_1], but coupling to the room is weak across R=1.65 m²K/W and it may forgo beneficial winter gains in a mixed NYC climate—net annual energy benefit is uncertain or small compared with interior-adjacent placement.
Mid-insulation placement suffers from small interface temperature swings and shows minimal impact on annual heating/cooling loads even when Tt cycles; mechanism demonstrated for X=0.5 placement.
